transitions.rationale: Create the new media_jobs table and indexes without changing existing tables, so the previous application remains compatible during migration and rollback.

Create the new media_download_jobs table and indexes only; existing media_jobs rows and schema are unchanged, so the previous application remains compatible during online expand and application rollback.

Add progress_stage (server default queued) and nullable cancel_requested_at. public_state stays on the PR9 allowlist; user cancellation is stored as expired + progress_stage=cancelled + cancel_requested_at so a rolled-back PR9 application can parse the row. A BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger maps progress_stage from public_state only when a previous PR9 application omits the new column (INSERT default or UPDATE that does not change progress_stage) and does not rewrite a legal PR10 cancellation encoding. Explicit illegal pairs still fail the CHECK. Previous application claim/retry/ready/failed/expiry UPDATEs and reads of PR10-cancelled rows therefore remain valid during online expand and application rollback.

Add nullable suggested_filename and progress_percent. Previous PR11 applications omit both columns on INSERT/UPDATE. A BEFORE UPDATE trigger clears progress_percent when progress_stage changes and NEW.progress_percent IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.progress_percent. PostgreSQL cannot distinguish an omitted column from an explicit assignment of the same value; both are normalized to NULL so a rolled-back PR11 application remains CHECK-compatible after a PR12 percent write. An explicit write of a different illegal percent still fails the CHECK. Same-stage percent updates are preserved. Downgrade drops the trigger, function, constraints, and columns without rewriting public_state.

Create the new media_delivery_grants table and indexes only. Existing media_download_jobs / media_jobs schema, enums, and CHECKs are unchanged, so a previous application that ignores the new table remains compatible during online expand and application rollback. Downgrade drops only the new grant objects.

Create anonymous_clients and free_download_quota_entries with indexes and constraints only. Existing media, download, and delivery-grant tables are unchanged, so the previous application ignores the additive schema safely during migration and rollback. Admission remains disabled by default until a separate operator activation.

Create the new payment_orders table, its private invoice sequence, indexes, and constraints only. Existing application tables and columns remain unchanged, so the previous application safely ignores the additive schema during migration and application rollback. Robokassa remains disabled by default and test activation is a separate deploy-time operation.

Create the new premium_entitlements table and indexes only. Existing payment_orders rows and application behavior remain unchanged until a new application issues entitlements on ResultURL. No entitlement data is backfilled by migration.

Create the bounded free_download_delivery_ranges ledger and indexes only. Existing quota entries and jobs are not rewritten; the default compatibility mode preserves READY-time consumption while old and new application revisions coexist.
